card.title: rDNA pipeline — cut, paste, copy, separate

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Recombinant DNA technology cuts and pastes genes across species: restriction endonucleases (molecular scissors, palindromic sites, sticky ends — EcoRI's GAATTC), vectors (plasmid pBR322, λ phage: origin + selectable markers + cloning sites), competent hosts (CaCl₂-treated E. coli take up DNA). The process chain runs DNA isolation → PCR amplification → gel electrophoresis separation → ligation → transformation → selection. PCR alone (denature–anneal–extend ×30 ≈ billion copies) revolutionised diagnostics and forensics.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: EcoRI: 5′-G|AATTC-3′ (sticky ends ligate)  ·  vector: ori + ampᴿ/tetᴿ markers + MCS  ·  PCR: 94 °C denature → ~54 °C anneal → 72 °C extend (Taq polymerase), 2ⁿ copies  ·  gel: DNA (−) migrates to anode; small fragments run farthest (EtBr/UV visualisation)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Restriction needs its exact palindrome (one-base mismatch usually blocks). Ligation needs compatible (sticky or blunt) ends plus ligase + ATP. Competence needs divalent cations + heat shock. PCR needs primers flanking the target, dNTPs and a thermostable polymerase.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Blue-white screening: insert disrupts lacZα → white recombinant colonies, blue non-recombinants. Agrobacterium Ti plasmid transforms plants naturally (crown gall → biotechnology's plant vector). Biolistics fires DNA-coated tungsten into cells that resist infection.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Clone a human gene into E. coli: isolate donor + plasmid DNA → cut both with EcoRI (matching sticky ends) → ligate → transform competent E. coli → plate on ampicillin+X-gal → pick white ampicillin-resistant colonies → verify insert by gel. Seven steps, each with its tool named.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Bacteria cannot post-translate like eukaryotes (glycosylation gaps — insulin needed engineering). Restriction sites may chop inside the gene of interest. PCR amplifies contamination equally (sterile technique critical). Antibiotic markers raise biosafety eyebrows.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From the central dogma outward: isolate the coding DNA, amplify the signal (PCR exponential: N = N₀·2ⁿ), separate by size (gel mobility ∝ 1/log(bp)), paste into a replicating vector, and let bacterial binary fission mass-produce the product — each tool solves one bottleneck in the DNA-to-product pipeline.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Tool chant: scissors (restriction) – vehicle (vector) – host (competent E. coli) – copier (PCR) – sorter (gel). PCR temperatures: 94–54–72. Gel reading: small = far. Selection: antibiotic resistance + blue-white.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: restriction/vector/host roles with one example each; PCR three steps with temperatures + 2ⁿ math; gel-electrophoresis separation logic; complete rDNA cloning flowchart.
